proof: For cube[-1,1]^3, the center piece satisfies all eight signed inequalities sx*x+sy*y+sz*z<=1, so equals |x|+|y|+|z|<=1. It is the regular octahedron A. In particular, intersecting the original front face y=-1 with this region forces x=z=0: the square face has only its center remaining, not an octagonal face. Wrong C retains an octagonal original-face remnant, which corresponds to shallower cuts. Both the source square face and distractor octagonal face are already-existing geometry and remain exactly in their original locations. Red outlines add no plane, cut, equality or new physical boundary; the colored polygon on the source is the original cube face, not a proposed cut. A human can still check every specified adjacent vertex and determine the octahedron uniquely.
